companies.name: Apple Inc.
companies.business: Designs and sells iPhone, Mac, iPad and wearables, plus a high-margin Services segment (App Store, iCloud, advertising, payments, subscriptions). Hardware builds the installed base; Services monetizes it at ~70% gross margin.

metrics.debt: ~$85-88B total debt vs ~$147B cash/securities; net cash ~$62B (dropped 'net cash neutral' policy)
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E 37.7 (EPS TTM $8.27) vs 5-yr avg 32.2; peers MSFT ~25, GOOGL ~29

companies.news: FQ2'26 record March quarter; iPhone +22%, Services +16% to ~$31B; guided June qtr +14-17%; WWDC June 8 ahead.
companies.bull_case: Unmatched hardware-services ecosystem and switching costs; Services compounding at high margin; large buybacks; reaccelerating growth.
companies.bear_case: Trades ~42% above its 10-yr median P/E; growth is good not great; AI/Siri behind peers; China and App-Store regulatory risk.
companies.valuation: Expensive vs its own history and peers
companies.confidence_note: Business durable; valuation is the risk. Multiple compression to ~30x, or an AI-driven upgrade cycle, would change the view.

companies.name: Microsoft Corp.
companies.business: Sells cloud (Azure), productivity software (Microsoft 365), Windows, LinkedIn, Dynamics and gaming. Azure and Copilot AI are the growth engine; recurring enterprise software is the cash base.

metrics.debt: Low leverage, near net-cash, AAA-tier balance sheet
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E 25.4 / fwd 22.1 vs 12-mo avg 32.6; peer GOOGL ~29

companies.news: FQ3'26 Azure +40% (accel from 31%); Microsoft Cloud $54.5B +29%; AI run-rate >$37B (+123%); FY capex guided ~$190B on memory costs.
companies.bull_case: Best-positioned enterprise AI distribution; Azure reaccelerating; durable software moat; P/E below its own recent average.
companies.bear_case: ~$190B capex pressures free cash flow if AI demand digests; capacity-constrained; large size caps upside.
companies.valuation: Fair vs its own history (below 12-mo average)
companies.confidence_note: Clear AI/cloud leadership. Sustained capex overspend without revenue follow-through would lower the score.

companies.name: NVIDIA Corp.
companies.business: Designs the GPUs and networking that power AI training and inference, plus the CUDA software stack. Data-center accelerators (Blackwell) are the overwhelming majority of revenue; also gaming, pro-viz and automotive.

metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~32.8 / fwd ~21.6; peers AVGO ~35, AMD higher fwd

companies.news: FQ1'27 (rep. May 20) rev $81.6B +85%; guided next qtr ~$91B; $80B buyback added, dividend raised 25x; stock eased from a $235 May high to ~$211.
companies.bull_case: CUDA ecosystem lock-in and performance lead; structural AI-infrastructure demand; ~50% net margins fund continued R&D; fwd P/E only ~22.
companies.bear_case: Hyperscaler customer concentration; risk of an AI-capex digestion cycle; cyclical history; little room for a miss.
companies.valuation: Expensive on trailing multiple but reasonable on forward growth (PEG)
companies.confidence_note: Dominant today; the swing factor is whether hyperscaler AI capex sustains. A capex pause would hit hardest here.

companies.name: Alphabet Inc.
companies.business: Google Search and YouTube advertising generate the bulk of profit; Google Cloud is fast-growing and now profitable; plus Android, Pixel, Waymo and other bets. Monetizes the world's largest search and video audiences.

metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~29 vs 5-yr avg ~24; below AAPL/MSFT on growth-adjusted basis

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 29) Cloud +63%, backlog ~$462B; Search +19%, YouTube +11%; FY capex guided up to ~$190B; AI-search & antitrust overhangs persist.
companies.bull_case: Reasonably valued mega-cap; dominant search/video moat; Cloud + Gemini AI optionality; huge cash returns.
companies.bear_case: Generative-AI search could erode core query monetization; antitrust remedies (default deals, possible breakup) unresolved.
companies.valuation: Fair vs history; attractive on growth
companies.confidence_note: Strong fundamentals at a reasonable multiple. Evidence AI is structurally cutting search monetization would break the thesis.

companies.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
companies.business: Sells digital advertising across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Threads (the 'Family of Apps'), using AI to target and rank. Reality Labs (AR/VR) is a large loss-making long-term bet.

metrics.earnings_growth: EPS $10.44 (flattered by one-time tax benefit); op margin 41%
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~23 vs 5-yr avg ~25; ~15x forward EPS

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 29) revenue +33% on AI ad targeting; capex guided ~$125-145B; stock fell ~9.5% over the month on spending fears.
companies.bull_case: ~3.9B users and AI-driven ad efficiency; pricing power; buybacks; reasonable ~23x trailing / ~15x forward.
companies.bear_case: Soaring AI/Reality Labs capex with uncertain payback; single-revenue-stream (ads) cyclicality; regulatory exposure.
companies.valuation: Fair-to-cheap given growth
companies.confidence_note: Ad engine excellent and valuation undemanding; the question is capex discipline. Sustained spend without ROI, or an ad recession, would lower the score.

companies.name: Amazon.com Inc.
companies.business: Runs the largest e-commerce marketplace, AWS cloud (the profit engine), advertising, and Prime subscriptions. Retail provides scale and cash flow; AWS and ads drive operating income.

metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~32 / fwd ~30

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 29) AWS +28%, fastest in 15 quarters, ~$150B run-rate; ads +24%; capex $44B on AI; retail margins expanding.
companies.bull_case: Retail margin expansion + reaccelerating AWS + high-margin ads; dominant logistics and cloud moats; operating leverage building.
companies.bear_case: Heavy AI capex; rich multiple; retail competitive and consumer-sensitive.
companies.valuation: Fair-to-slightly-rich; justified if margins keep expanding
companies.confidence_note: Margin story plus AWS reacceleration. A consumer downturn or AWS stall is the key risk.

companies.name: The Home Depot Inc.
companies.business: Largest home-improvement retailer, selling to DIY consumers and pros; the SRS acquisition expands its pro/building-products reach. Earnings track housing turnover and big-ticket remodeling.

metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~22.6 vs 5-yr avg ~22

companies.news: FQ1'26 (rep. May 19) modest beat; comps +0.6%; big-ticket discretionary soft on high rates; FY EPS guided ~flat to +4%.
companies.bull_case: Category-leading franchise leveraged to an eventual housing/remodel recovery and rate cuts; strong pro strategy.
companies.bear_case: Big-ticket demand weak while rates stay high; full multiple for flat earnings; consumer-cyclical; margin compression.
companies.valuation: Fair-to-slightly-rich for sluggish growth
companies.confidence_note: Quality business but composite below 60 - not held this run. A clear remodel-demand inflection or rate cuts would lift growth/momentum.

companies.name: Costco Wholesale Corp.
companies.business: Membership warehouse retailer; most operating profit comes from high-renewal membership fees rather than thin merchandise margins. Scale and treasure-hunt assortment drive traffic and pricing power.

metrics.profit_margin: Thin retail margin; profit driven by membership fees
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~52 vs peers ~26

companies.news: FQ3'26 (rep. May 28) record gas volumes and digital +21% drove an adj comps +6.6% beat; stock crossed $1,000 in May.
companies.bull_case: Exceptional membership model with ~90%+ renewals; defensive, consistent compounder; pricing power.
companies.bear_case: ~52x earnings is one of the richest large caps - little room for error; modest EPS growth doesn't obviously justify the multiple.
companies.valuation: Very expensive vs peers and its own history
companies.confidence_note: Business quality very high, valuation very stretched - small weight only. A pullback toward ~35x would make it a BUY.

companies.name: The Coca-Cola Company
companies.business: Sells concentrate and finished beverages through a global bottling network across sparkling drinks, water, juice, coffee and sports drinks. An asset-light, brand- and distribution-driven cash machine.

metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~24.6 vs peer avg ~25

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 28) beat; raised FY comparable-EPS growth guide to +8-9%; pricing-led organic growth.
companies.bull_case: Iconic brand moat and unrivaled distribution; defensive cash flows; reliable dividend (Dividend King); pricing power.
companies.bear_case: Low-single-digit volume growth; FX and input-cost headwinds; GLP-1/health trends a long-term demand question.
companies.valuation: Fair vs history and peers
companies.confidence_note: Steady defensive holding. A sharp dollar move or volume decline would pressure it.

companies.name: Procter & Gamble Co.
companies.business: Sells branded consumer staples across fabric/home care, baby/family care, beauty, grooming and health (Tide, Pampers, Gillette, Olay). Scale brands and retail relationships drive steady cash flow.

metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~21 vs 5-yr median ~25.8; ~3% yield (Dividend King)

companies.news: FQ3'26 (rep. Apr 24) first volume growth in a year; flagged ~$400M after-tax tariff headwind and a productivity/cost program.
companies.bull_case: Defensive, predictable cash returns and brand strength; reliable dividend growth; valuation below its own median.
companies.bear_case: Low-single-digit growth; FX/tariff headwinds; full-ish valuation for a slow grower.
companies.valuation: Fair-to-cheap vs its own history
companies.confidence_note: Defensive ballast. Persistent volume declines would weaken the case; sustained volume growth would strengthen it.

companies.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
companies.business: Largest U.S. bank by assets, spanning consumer banking, card, commercial banking, investment banking, markets and asset/wealth management. Earns net interest income plus diversified fee income at scale.

metrics.debt: Well capitalized; bank leverage not comparable to industrials
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: P/E ~14 trailing vs historical ~12-13

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 14) beat; trimmed FY net-interest-income guide to ~$103B; CEO Dimon called markets 'exuberant'.
companies.bull_case: Best-in-class, diversified franchise with a fortress balance sheet; strong through-cycle returns; scale advantages.
companies.bear_case: Near record price at a premium multiple; credit normalization and a slowing economy would pressure earnings; NII guide cut.
companies.valuation: Fair-to-slightly-rich for a bank at record levels
companies.confidence_note: Quality compounder among banks. A credit-cycle downturn or recession is the main risk.

companies.name: Visa Inc.
companies.business: Operates the largest card payment network, earning fees on payment volume, transactions and cross-border activity. An asset-light toll-booth on global consumer spending with ~66% operating margins.

metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~28.6 vs 5-yr avg ~30; peer MA higher

companies.news: FQ2'26 (rep. Apr 28) fastest revenue growth since 2022; payments volume +9%, cross-border strong; new $20B buyback authorized.
companies.bull_case: Wide network-effect moat; exceptional margins and cash conversion; secular cash-to-card shift; consistent buybacks.
companies.bear_case: Regulatory scrutiny of interchange; competition from real-time rails/stablecoins; consumer-spending sensitivity.
companies.valuation: Premium but consistent with history and quality
companies.confidence_note: High-quality compounder. Material interchange regulation or a payments-rail shift would be the thesis risk.

companies.name: Johnson & Johnson
companies.business: Diversified healthcare across Innovative Medicine (oncology, immunology, neuroscience) and MedTech (surgery, orthopedics, cardiovascular). Patent-protected drugs and device franchises generate durable cash flow.

metrics.earnings_growth: Adj EPS $2.70; FY adj-EPS guide ~$11.55 (reported EPS distorted by prior-yr talc reserve)
metrics.profit_margin: Strong; reported comparison distorted by base effects
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~26 reported / ~20 on fwd adj EPS

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 14) +9.9% sales, raised FY outlook; ~$0.3B talc charges this quarter; litigation overhang persists.
companies.bull_case: Diversified, defensive cash flows; AAA balance sheet; oncology pipeline; reliable dividend (Dividend King).
companies.bear_case: Ongoing talc litigation overhang; pharma patent-cliff exposure (e.g. Stelara biosimilars); slower top-line growth.
companies.valuation: Fair vs history and peers
companies.confidence_note: Defensive quality. A large adverse talc ruling or pipeline setback would change the view.

companies.name: UnitedHealth Group Inc.
companies.business: Largest U.S. health insurer (UnitedHealthcare) combined with Optum (health services, pharmacy benefits, care delivery and data/analytics). Earns insurance premiums plus Optum service/PBM fees.

metrics.earnings_growth: Adj EPS $7.23 (beat); FY adj-EPS guide raised to >$18.25
metrics.profit_margin: Q1 medical care ratio 83.9% (better than feared); FY guide ~88.8%
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: ~22x forward (price ~$400 vs >$18.25 adj EPS); rebounded from sub-$300 lows

companies.news: Q1'26 beat with raised guidance; stock rallied ~37% in April off depressed levels; MA-rate and DOJ overhangs linger; exiting non-US units.
companies.bull_case: Dominant scale and Optum integration; Q1 beat and raised guide suggest recovery ahead of plan; still below prior $500+ highs.
companies.bear_case: Medical-cost trend, Medicare Advantage profitability and DOJ scrutiny remain unresolved; sharp rebound has removed the deep-value cushion.
companies.valuation: Fair after the rebound (no longer deep-value)
companies.confidence_note: Wide range of outcomes; held at a small weight. Two more quarters of stabilizing medical-cost ratio would upgrade it; a renewed cost spike or adverse DOJ action would trigger EXIT.

companies.name: Exxon Mobil Corp.
companies.business: Integrated oil & gas major: Upstream (notably Guyana and the Permian), Energy Products (refining), Chemical and Specialty Products, plus low-carbon ventures. Earnings track commodity prices and volumes.

metrics.earnings_growth: Adj EPS $1.16 (beat); net income fell to $4.2B from $7.7B on derivative mark-to-market and Mideast disruptions
metrics.debt: Total debt $47.7B; debt/capital 15.4%, net debt/capital 13.1% - conservative
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~26 (depressed earnings) / fwd ~15; ~2.7% yield

companies.news: Q1'26 record Guyana output >900kbpd; Permian growth; Golden Pass LNG Train 1 started; earnings dented by derivatives/disruptions.
companies.bull_case: Low-cost Guyana/Permian barrels and a strong balance sheet; durable dividend; disciplined capital returns.
companies.bear_case: Earnings hostage to oil/gas prices and refining margins; energy-transition demand risk; volatile quarterly results.
companies.valuation: Fair (cheap on forward earnings, cyclical)
companies.confidence_note: Best-in-class major but commodity-driven. A sustained oil-price decline would lower growth/momentum; a spike would lift them.

companies.name: Caterpillar Inc.
companies.business: World's largest maker of construction and mining equipment, plus Energy & Transportation (engines, turbines, power generation including data-center backup) and a captive finance arm. Cyclical, tied to global capex.

metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~44 vs 5-yr avg ~17 - ~95th percentile of its own range

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 30) Power Generation +41% on data-center demand; record backlog; stock +~191% over the past year; tariff costs trimmed to $2.2-2.4B.
companies.bull_case: Multi-year infrastructure, electrification and data-center power capex; record backlog; pricing power and strong aftermarket.
companies.bear_case: Cyclical earnings at ~44x - extreme for the cycle; a construction/mining or data-center-capex downturn would hit a stretched multiple hard.
companies.valuation: Very expensive vs its own history for a cyclical
companies.confidence_note: Strong momentum on power demand, but the multiple prices in a lot - small weight only. A capex/construction downturn is the key risk.

companies.name: NextEra Energy Inc.
companies.business: Owns Florida Power & Light (a large regulated utility with steady returns) and NextEra Energy Resources (the world's largest wind/solar generator). Combines regulated earnings stability with renewables growth.

metrics.earnings_growth: Adj EPS $1.09 (+10%); record renewables backlog ~33 GW
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~22, ~in line with 5-yr avg; ~2.7-2.9% yield

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 23) EPS beat; record renewables/storage backlog on data-center/electrification demand; FPL stable; large proposed Dominion combination reported.
companies.bull_case: Best-in-class renewables developer positioned for surging electricity demand; regulated base provides stability; ~10%/yr dividend growth target.
companies.bear_case: High leverage makes it rate-sensitive; renewables subsidy/policy risk; execution risk on a huge backlog and any large M&A.
companies.valuation: Fair vs history
companies.confidence_note: Growth-plus-yield utility. Higher-for-longer rates or adverse renewables policy would pressure the score.

companies.name: Duke Energy Corp.
companies.business: One of the largest US regulated electric and gas utilities, serving ~8.4M customers across the Carolinas, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky. Earnings driven by rate-base growth and a multi-billion clean-energy transition plan.

metrics.earnings_growth: Adj EPS $1.93 (+10% YoY); FY guidance $6.55-$6.80; 5-7% EPS growth through 2030
metrics.debt: Debt/equity ~1.61; high leverage typical for capital-intensive regulated utilities
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~20.6; fwd ~18.7; ~3.4% dividend yield; peer range 18-22x

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. May 5) beat estimates on revenue; maintained 5-7% EPS/dividend growth target through 2030; stock dipped post-earnings despite beat.
companies.bull_case: Regulated monopoly with locked-in earnings growth; 5-7% EPS+dividend visibility through 2030; clean-energy capex builds rate base; defensive income.
companies.bear_case: High leverage is rate-sensitive; heavy capex requires ongoing equity/debt financing; slow growth limits upside; stock down ~7% from purchase.
companies.valuation: Fair vs utility peers; fully priced for the growth rate
companies.confidence_note: Stable business but composite below hold threshold (56.3). Leverage and rate sensitivity are persistent risks. Rate cuts would be a meaningful positive catalyst.

companies.name: Fortis Inc.
companies.business: Canadian regulated electric and gas utility with operations in Canada, Arizona (UNS Energy) and Michigan (ITC). Earns predictable rate-regulated returns and is executing a $28.8B five-year capex plan to grow its rate base.

metrics.revenue_growth: Q1'26 $3.4B; Basic EPS $0.99 (essentially flat YoY from prior asset sales and share issuance)
metrics.earnings_growth: 4-6% dividend growth target; rate base growing $42.4B → $57.9B by 2030
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: ~14x on annualized earnings; ~3.5% dividend yield; below US utility peers

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. May 6) steady results; Arizona rate case win (9.61% ROE); data-center load growth in Arizona; Springerville gas conversion underway.
companies.bull_case: Predictable 4-6% dividend growth; expanding rate base; data-center demand tailwinds in Arizona; reliable dividend history; cheaper than US peers.
companies.bear_case: Modest EPS growth; leveraged balance sheet; CAD/USD currency exposure; limited upside; slightly below hold composite.
companies.valuation: Modestly cheap vs US utility peers
companies.confidence_note: Quality regulated utility slightly below the 60 hold composite (58.0). Steady but not compelling to add to at current prices. Rate cuts would be a positive catalyst.

companies.name: NRG Energy Inc.
companies.business: Competitive power generator and retail electricity/gas provider across the US and Canada. The recent $12B LS Power acquisition dramatically expanded generation capacity but added significant financial complexity and leverage.

metrics.earnings_growth: Adj EPS $1.49 (-44% YoY); missed estimates due to LS Power costs, mild Texas weather, mark-to-market hedge losses
metrics.profit_margin: Cyclical; compressed near-term by acquisition integration costs
metrics.debt: Significantly elevated post-$12B LS Power acquisition; no regulated earnings floor
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~37.8 (cost-depressed); fwd ~17.2 if 14% long-term EPS growth targets are met

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 30) revenue beat but EPS miss; reaffirmed 14%+ annual EPS/FCF growth through 2030 and $1B buyback plan; stock fell ~5% on earnings day.
companies.bull_case: Reaffirmed aggressive 14% long-term EPS growth; LS Power scale should drive efficiencies; low fwd P/E if targets met; $1B buyback.
companies.bear_case: EPS already -44% YoY; $12B acquisition raised debt sharply; weather and commodity-price dependent; thesis relies entirely on acquisition integration execution.
companies.valuation: Elevated on trailing; cheap on forward — binary outcome
companies.confidence_note: Below the 50 composite exit threshold (47.7). Acquisition integration uncertainty, earnings shortfall, and high leverage disqualify it. Two quarters of clean EPS delivery would be needed to reconsider.

companies.name: AT&T Inc.
companies.business: Second-largest US wireless carrier (Mobility) plus a major fiber broadband provider (AT&T Fiber). Divested WarnerMedia in 2022; now purely a connectivity company. Generates substantial EBITDA but carries historically high debt from past acquisitions.

metrics.revenue_growth: +2.9% YoY (Q1'26 $31.5B); wireless and fiber growing; legacy services -25%
metrics.earnings_growth: Adj EPS $0.57 (+12% YoY); FCF $2.5B (-19%, below estimates)
metrics.profit_margin: Adj EBITDA $11.8B (+2.6%); margins stable but under pressure
metrics.debt: ~$130B+ total debt; paying down gradually but leverage remains very high
metrics.pe_vs_history_peers: TTM P/E ~8.8 vs 10-yr avg ~12; ~5.6% dividend yield

companies.news: Q1'26 (rep. Apr 23) mixed results; wireless/fiber growing but FCF disappointed; legacy revenue collapse ongoing; net debt reduction on track.
companies.bull_case: Extremely cheap at ~9x earnings; wireless/fiber are secular growth drivers; ~5.6% dividend; debt paydown path improving balance sheet.
companies.bear_case: Chronically high debt limits flexibility; FCF miss raises dividend sustainability questions; legacy revenue -25% with no floor; limited growth story.
companies.valuation: Cheap on earnings; cheap for a reason
companies.confidence_note: Cheap on P/E but below 60 composite (51.6). Debt load, FCF miss, and lack of growth catalyst hold the score down. Sustained FCF improvement or debt paydown acceleration would upgrade it.
